request.instructions:
You are Ghostline, an experimental scientist that works through a camera. The human is your hands: they film; you measure, model, and decide what to film next.

Your job is to find which candidate model explains the physical system in the video, and to say honestly when the evidence is not sufficient.

Rules:
- Never state a number that did not come from a tool result. When you give a number, it must be traceable to a specific tool output in this conversation.
- Never claim a model is correct because it fits the training data. Only holdout predictions and pre-committed predictions count as evidence.
- Always call `check_validity` after `measure`. If validity is `invalid`, stop: explain why in plain language and tell the user how to re-film. Do not fit or score invalid data.
- When the comparison is `ambiguous`, say so plainly ("Inconclusive"), then (when asked what to do next) call `design_experiment` and then `commit_predictions` BEFORE asking the user to film anything.
- Reveal runs are never refit. Score them only with `evaluate_commitment`.
- Call `render_ghosts` so the user can see each model's prediction over the video.
- Keep user-facing explanations short, concrete, and in plain language. Lead with the verdict. Use at most 5 sentences in your final message.
- Before each tool call, write one short sentence saying what you are about to check and why (this is shown to the user as your lab notebook).

- Write plain text for a lab notebook: no LaTeX, no $...$ math, no markdown headings. Use unicode (θ, ω₀, σ, °) and keep each message under ~120 words.
- If a verdict has `all_models_inadequate: true`, lead with that: name the least-wrong model, but say plainly that none of the candidates describes this system and quote `inadequacy_note` (it includes `likely_cause` when a validity check found one).

input.content: Analyze run run_a_8deg of experiment exp_pendulum_a (a pendulum experiment). Measure it, check validity, fit the candidate models, compare them on held-out data, and render the ghosts. Then tell me whether the evidence is decisive, in plain language.

content.text: I will look at the keyframes first to confirm what to track in this pendulum run.

input.output: {"system_type": "pendulum", "tracked_concepts": ["orange ball"], "reference_object": {"concept": "green disk", "known_size_m": 0.02426, "dimension": "diameter"}, "anchor_hint": "pivot at top center", "gravity_direction_hint": "down", "notes": "small-angle pendulum with orange bob", "confidence": 0.95, "backend": "Muse Spark (muse-spark-1.3) via Meta Model API"}

content.text: Scene confirmed as a pendulum, now I will track the orange ball through the video.
Tracking finished, now I will convert the tracks to a calibrated angle time series.
Measurement done, now I will check whether the recording can be trusted.

input.output: {"status": "valid", "checks": [{"name": "camera_drift", "status": "pass", "reason": "Reference object stayed within 1.0 px of its starting position."}, {"name": "camera_jump", "status": "pass", "reason": "No sudden camera jumps."}, {"name": "scale_changed", "status": "pass", "reason": "Scale stable (reference size varied 2.7%)."}, {"name": "tracking_lost", "status": "pass", "reason": "Object tracked in 100.0% of the evaluation frames."}, {"name": "frame_timing", "status": "pass", "reason": "Frame timing regular (median 60.0 fps)."}, {"name": "pendulum_geometry", "status": "pass", "reason": "Bob moves on a circular arc (residual 0.64 px, length 0.637 m)."}, {"name": "object_shape", "status": "pass", "reason": "The tracked object keeps a steady outline (size varies 5%)."}]}

content.text: Recording is valid, now I will list the candidate pendulum models to fit.

input.output: {"models": [{"name": "pendulum_linear", "equation": "\\ddot\\theta + 2\\gamma\\dot\\theta + \\omega_0^2\\,\\theta = 0", "params": ["omega0", "gamma", "theta0", "dtheta0"], "knob_transfer": "omega0 and gamma are properties of the pendulum and stay fixed; the new initial state comes from the conditioning window"}, {"name": "pendulum_nonlinear", "equation": "\\ddot\\theta + 2\\gamma\\dot\\theta + \\omega_0^2\\,\\sin\\theta = 0", "params": ["omega0", "gamma", "theta0", "dtheta0"], "knob_transfer": "omega0 and gamma are properties of the pendulum and stay fixed; the new initial state comes from the conditioning window"}, {"name": "pendulum_nonlinear_quaddamp", "equation": "\\ddot\\theta + c\\,\\dot\\theta|\\dot\\theta| + \\omega_0^2\\,\\sin\\theta = 0", "params": ["omega0", "c", "theta0", "dtheta0"], "knob_transfer": "omega0 and gamma are properties of the pendulum and stay fixed; the new initial state comes from the conditioning window"}]}

content.text: I have three candidates, now I will fit them on training data and score them on held-out data.

input.output: {"note": "fitted on training window only; holdout scored with frozen parameters", "fits": [{"model": "pendulum_linear", "params": {"omega0": 4.04, "gamma": 0.03013, "theta0": 0.131, "dtheta0": 0.000975}, "param_std": {"omega0": 0.000428, "gamma": 0.0004044, "theta0": 0.0002111, "dtheta0": 0.0008806}, "train_rmse": 0.001481, "holdout_rmse": 0.001645, "bic": -5605.0, "ljung_box_p": 0.1546, "n_train": 432, "n_holdout": 288}, {"model": "pendulum_nonlinear", "params": {"omega0": 4.043, "gamma": 0.03013, "theta0": 0.131, "dtheta0": 0.0005001}, "param_std": {"omega0": 0.0003765, "gamma": 0.0004358, "theta0": 0.0002134, "dtheta0": 0.0008753}, "train_rmse": 0.001477, "holdout_rmse": 0.001658, "bic": -5607.0, "ljung_box_p": 0.1485, "n_train": 432, "n_holdout": 288}, {"model": "pendulum_nonlinear_quaddamp", "params": {"omega0": 4.043, "c": 0.149, "theta0": 0.1315, "dtheta0": 0.000598}, "param_std": {"omega0": 0.0004245, "c": 0.002005, "theta0": 0.0002221, "dtheta0": 0.0008515}, "train_rmse": 0.001483, "holdout_rmse": 0.001858, "bic": -5603.0, "ljung_box_p": 0.1227, "n_train": 432, "n_holdout": 288}]}

tools.name: describe_scene
tools.description: Understand the scene from keyframes: system type, what to track, reference object of known size.

tools.name: track_objects
tools.description: Track the moving object and the reference object through the video (SAM 3.1 or fallback tracker).

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Convert tracks into calibrated physical time series (theta(t) or y(t)), estimate noise, fix the train/holdout split.

tools.name: check_validity
tools.description: Check whether the recording can be trusted (camera moved, scale changed, tracking lost, timing, setup mismatch).

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List candidate dynamical models for a system type.

tools.name: fit_models
tools.description: Fit candidate models on the TRAINING part of the run only, then score them on the held-out part.

tools.name: compare_models
tools.description: Compare fitted models on holdout evidence; returns decisive/ambiguous with the numbers behind it.

tools.name: discover_equation
tools.description: Sparse equation discovery (PySINDy) on the training data, as supporting evidence.

tools.name: design_experiment
tools.description: Find the experimental setting (knob value) that best separates the candidate models.

tools.name: commit_predictions
tools.description: Freeze each model's predictions for the proposed experiment and publish a SHA-256 commitment BEFORE the user films it.

tools.name: evaluate_commitment
tools.description: Score a new (reveal) run against a commitment: verify hash, check validity, condition on the first 0.5 s only, compare predictions.

tools.name: render_ghosts
tools.description: Render each model's prediction as a translucent ghost over the video.
